Exercice
Build an error monitor workflow
VÉRIFICATION INTELLIGENTE

A scheduled job keeps blowing up on a field that isn't there — and the best signal you get is a red execution badge. Operators need context: which workflow failed, what broke, and where it happened.

Import the fragile starter, then create a separate Error Monitor workflow with an Error Trigger, Edit Fields to shape the payload, and a Data Table insert into error_log. Set it as the fragile workflow's Error Workflow and activate to confirm failures land in the table.

Exercice
Route HTTP errors instead of stopping
VÉRIFICATION INTELLIGENTE

This workflow calls an API that sometimes answers with HTTP 500. Out of the box, n8n stops the whole run right there — so you capture nothing useful and anything downstream never fires.

Import the starter, set HTTP Request to Continue Using Error Output, and route the red error path into Edit Fields so failures get logged without killing the execution.

Instructions
100XP

1

2

3

4

Create a new workflow, then import 4.1.3_starter_failing-node-workflow.json from Desktop > Resources.
Execute the workflow and confirm the run stops at the HTTP Request node.
In HTTP Request Output or the execution error details, confirm the request to https://httpstat.us/500 failed.

VÉRIFICATION INTELLIGENTE

Nobody can see how many records actually made it through each stage of the ingestion run — and you don't want to reshape the main pipeline just to find out. A side-branch audit trail tracks progress without disrupting the data flow.

Import the starter, create an execution_log table, and add Data Table insert nodes as side branches off HTTP Request, Transform Data, and Format Output. Finish with Get row(s) to verify that three checkpoint rows land in the table.

Exercice
Build an output evaluation quality gate
VÉRIFICATION INTELLIGENTE

After formatting, leadership wants an explicit pass-or-fail — not another questionable batch sliding toward the next step. Bad data should show up on a branch you can actually see.

Pick up from your logging exercise (or import its solution). Layer in Code as Evaluate Output, split with If on pass, and wire Edit Fields on each branch so $('Evaluate Output') carries the right totals and issues into the summaries.

Instructions
100XP

1

2

3

4

5

If you've got the workflow open from the previous exercise, continue below.
If you need to reload it, import 4.2.1_solution_logging-checkpoints.json from Desktop > Resources. If loading fresh, ensure the execution_log data table exists (columns: step string, item_count number, timestamp string), then open each Data Table node and re-select execution_log in the table picker.
Delete the Read Log node (you will replace that inspection step with the new quality gate).

Exercice
Assemble the end-to-end capstone pipeline
VÉRIFICATION INTELLIGENTE

Stakeholders want one scheduled workflow that pulls weather, normalizes it, skips duplicates, batches the rest, checks quality, and separates clean results from failures — the full toolkit from this chapter on one canvas.

Build it from scratch: Schedule Trigger and HTTP Request for data ingestion, Code nodes for transforms and deduplication, Loop Over Items for batching, then an evaluation gate with If to split pass/fail outcomes.

Instructions
100XP

1

2

3

4

5

Create a new workflow.
Add a Schedule Trigger node and set the rule to Hours with every 1 hour.
Add an HTTP Request node, set Method to GET, and use the URL https://wttr.in/London?format=j1. Under Options > Response, set Response Format to JSON.
Execute the workflow and confirm parsed JSON weather data appears in Output.
